instantiated_cells.justification: Principals must file expense statements on or before July 31 and January 31 (semiannual), not annually.
The statute specifies filings due July 31 and January 31, not monthly reporting.
The only periodic deadlines stated are July 31 and January 31, so no other reporting frequency option is provided.
Expense statements are required twice per year rather than quarterly.
Registered principals must file an expense statement by July 31 and January 31 covering each preceding 6-month reporting period.
Reporting periods are defined as 6-month periods and statements are due twice yearly, not tri-annually linked to the legislative calendar.
Because the statute specifies only semiannual filing dates, there is no 'other' reporting frequency to describe.
The registration statement must include a description of the business activity (or nature and purposes) of the principal, disclosing what type of business/organization it is.
The expense statement’s aggregate total must include compensation to lobbyists for lobbying (cash or in-kind).
Principals must report the name of each official/candidate reimbursed under §13.625(7) along with the date and amount, which is a contact-level disclosure.
Principals must report each legislative proposal, budget bill subject, proposed administrative rule number, or otherwise each topic of lobbying communications with reasonable specificity.

The expense statement requires certain totals (e.g., aggregate lobbying expenditures, travel/living expenses, reimbursements) but does not require reporting gifts, entertainment, transportation, and lodging as such (and §13.625 largely prohibits them).
The statement includes non-compensation lobbying costs such as research/analysis, paid advertising to urge the public, and specified office overhead when lobbyists are in-house.
When payments to a lobbyist exceed $200, the principal must list the lobbyist’s name and address, but the statute does not require disclosure of the lobbyist’s phone number.
Principals must report aggregate lobbying expenditures for the principal and all lobbyists, and must list each lobbyist by name (and address) if paid over $200 in the period.
The bundled provisions specify registration and expense-statement contents but contain no requirement to disclose major financial contributors to the principal.
The principal’s registration statement must include the principal’s name and business address.
Principals must report each legislative proposal (i.e., bill/resolution), budget bill subject, and proposed administrative rule number connected to lobbying communications.
The statement must report the aggregate total lobbying expenditures and obligations for lobbying by the principal and all lobbyists for the principal.
Compensation to lobbyists must be included in total lobbying expenditures and, if payments to a lobbyist exceed $200 in the reporting period, the total amount paid to that lobbyist must be listed.
The statute requires daily itemization of time and itemized listings for certain lobbyist payments (over $200) and reimbursements (name/date/amount), not solely lump-sum reporting.
Associations must report the chief executive officer and approximate number of members, but there is no requirement to list names of all sponsors or members.

Because the expense statement covers lobbying by 'all lobbyists for the principal' and requires naming each lobbyist when payments exceed $200, the report includes listing employed/retained lobbyists at least above that threshold.
